_about: 757-200, from Boeing D6-58327 Rev H 2.2.1 (page index 19): side, plan and front views on one sheet. Pixels of layers.py rasters at scale 20, line centres. Scaled by the printed 46.97 m from the nose to the tail cone (the side view's dimension, line centre to line centre); the plan's 47.32 m overall length is to the fin tip's trailing corner. The sheet draws the cabin windows (thin strokes, closed outlines); seven behind the wing's lines are placed at the drawing's own pitch. The nacelle is the PW2000's (a short fan cowl, the core's nozzle behind). A plain wingtip: the document has no winglet sheet.

sources.title: Boeing, 757 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58327 Rev H, December 2024), 2.2.1 General Dimensions: Model 757-200, -200PF; 2.7.1 Door Clearances
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/b752/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. Plain wingtips (the document has no winglet sheet; many US 757-200s now fly with blended winglets, which this shape doesn't have) and the PW2000's nacelle (a short fan cowl, the core's nozzle behind; the RB211's is longer). The sheet draws the cabin windows; the seven behind the wing's lines in the drawing are placed at its own window pitch. Doors 1, 2 and 4 and the cargo doors sit within 1 cm of the door table (2.7.1). Checks over 1.5%: the side view draws the fuselage 4.19 m tall between its own dimension arrows, labelled 4.01 m (+4.5%), and its belly 0.12 m lower aft of the wing, so over the middle third it reads +6.0%; the plan's width is as printed and the front view's section is 3.93 m tall, so it's the side view's drawing, kept here. The front view draws the nacelle 2.34 m across where the sheet prints 2.46 m (RR) and 2.69 m (PW); kept the drawing's.
